basic_info.title: Avoiding Latent Variable Collapse With Generative Skip Models
basic_info.affiliation: Columbia University / Harvard University (consortium; not fully confirmed from abstract page)

venue.name: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2019)

method.notes: Proposes adding SKIP CONNECTIONS from the latent variable directly to the likelihood/decoder at every generation step (not just at the start), strengthening the statistical dependency between latent code and every output token/pixel. Proven (theoretically, via an information-theoretic argument) to increase mutual information between observations and the inferred latent, reducing collapse, while preserving predictive performance. Directly relevant to Stage-2's own architecture: the 'Heads reads (h, z) jointly, not h alone' design already implements this skip-connection idea at every timestep -- and this paper's own caveat (skip connections alone are insufficient under a sufficiently strong competing decoder input) is consistent with why Stage 2's existing (h,z)-joint heads did NOT prevent collapse once road_embed gave h a free deterministic channel. This paper rules out 'give heads more access to z' as a further fix -- that access already exists structurally; the redundancy is the problem, not reachability.

gap_analysis.whats_missing: Not a map-matching or pillar-novelty paper -- included as a Stage-2 architecture precedent, confirming what is already correctly implemented and why it alone is insufficient.
gap_analysis.novelty_reasoning: Relevant only to confirm Stage-2's existing (h,z)-joint decoder heads already implement this paper's fix, and that its own literature caveats explain why it did not, by itself, prevent posterior collapse once a competing deterministic channel (road_embed) was introduced.

relevance.bmw_relevance: Not directly BMW-relevant; cited as confirmation that Stage 2's architecture already satisfies this paper's recommended fix (skip/joint access to z), which rules out 'give heads more access to z' as a viable NEW lever and points fixes toward weakening h's competing input (Change 13A) or forcing z to solve something h cannot (Change 13B) instead.

uncertain: Whether Stage-2's specific (h,z) concatenation into each head exactly matches this paper's proposed skip-connection topology (vs. a superficially similar but mechanistically different design) was not independently verified beyond the analogy noted in stage2_correction.md.
